Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  • Sudden‐onset chest pressure/discomfort x 2 hours, constant, 7/10, central location (“like someone sitting on my chest”).  
  • Associated shortness of breath, light-headedness, nausea (no vomiting), left shoulder/arm pain.  
  • Hypertension and hypercholesterolemia (untreated).  
  • Reports calf pain and leg swelling with exertion.  
  • Smoker.  
- Relevant family medical history: Not recorded.  
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications): None reported; “No, I don’t take any medicine.”  
- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.  
- Sexual and reproductive health: Not recorded.  
- Physical activity and nutrition: Gardens fortnightly; currently limits activity to household mobility due to exertional breathlessness; diet not discussed.  
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use: Smokes (quantity/frequency not documented); alcohol and other substances not recorded.  
- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded.  
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk): No concerns raised; screening not performed.  
- Vision problems or recent changes: Not recorded.  
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities: Lives with wife; no caring or social support issues noted.

Examination

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded (telehealth; awaiting paramedics).  
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated): Not recorded.  
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums): Not performed.  
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed): Not performed.  
- Vision/eye exam (basic screen): Not performed.  
- Urinalysis (dipstick for proteinuria): Not performed.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed): Not ordered during this acute consult.  
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due): Not applicable (male).  
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35): Not indicated/discussed.  
- Mammogram (if eligible): Not applicable.  
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D): Not ordered.  

Management Plan

- Immediate ambulance activated; patient advised to remain on line until arrival.  
- Explained concern for possible cardiac etiology; emphasized urgency of hospital assessment.  
- Advised to stay calm, sit quietly, sip water; no medications to be taken prior to paramedic review.  
- Paramedics will obtain vitals, ECG, cardiac enzymes; hospital consultant to assess on arrival.  
- Clinician to arrange follow-up appointment after hospital evaluation.  
- Patient advised to inform wife and prepare essentials for hospital.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note):

● Missing but clinically expected elements: BP, heart rate, respiratory rate, O2 saturation, weight/BMI, waist circumference, comprehensive medication/allergy list, immunisation review, detailed alcohol intake, mental health screening, dietary assessment, domestic violence/social screening, hearing and vision checks, urinalysis, blood tests (BGL/lipids), cardiovascular risk calculation.  
● Internal contradictions: Age quoted as both 54 and “suppose I'd be 53” (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor speech overlaps and unfinished sentences but key clinical information intelligible.
